# Maintain DayQ Firearms

Read [FIREARM_MAINTENANCE_AND_FAMILIARITY_CONTRACT.md](references/FIREARM_MAINTENANCE_AND_FAMILIARITY_CONTRACT.md) completely before changing weapon, inventory, progression, animation, or repair code.

1. Inspect the current weapon component, persistent item schema, authoritative inventory transactions, crafting/repair jobs, progression evidence, animation layers, locomotion, acoustics, persistence journal, firearm asset job, and tests. Extend existing owners; do not create parallel truth.
2. Model every maintenance action as a server-authorized, interruption-safe state machine. The weapon, feed device, chamber state, removed components, cleaning supplies, tools, maintenance surface, work progress, faults, and output condition must remain exact through cancel, damage, movement, disconnect, restart, crash, rollback, and migration.
3. Drive the state machine from weapon-family Maintenance Profile Data Assets. Resolve shared mechanism profiles through `dayq/data/DAYQ_FIREARM_MAINTENANCE_PROFILE_INDEX.json`; every compatible family must map exactly once before runtime use. Profiles contain abstract, source-verified manipulation nodes, prerequisites, component relationships, hand occupancy, animation events, work envelopes, inspection visibility, fault exposure, and reassembly validation. Do not embed real-world instructional prose in UI, logs, schemas, or generated documentation.
4. Present maintenance in first person with real separated parts, authored pivots, hand contacts, a maintenance mat or supported surface, dirt/wear inspection, cleaning motion, repair substitution, and reassembly. Third-person proxies may simplify presentation but must project the same authoritative state and duration.
5. Make maintenance costly through time, exposure, consumable cleaning supplies, tool condition, workspace quality, material/print/fabrication jobs, component quality, diagnosis risk, and opportunity cost. Do not require scavenging an exact proprietary part when DayQ manufacturing can produce an appropriate replacement.
6. Require manufactured replacement parts to pass the existing fabrication tree: printer capability, material grade, forge/foundry feedstock where applicable, finishing/metrology, agent assistance, quality, and installation. A printable part is not automatically high-quality or immediately available.
7. Award server-measured familiarity from meaningful weapon use, varied maintenance, diagnosed faults, successful reassembly, combat handling, and training. Reject idle repetition, repeated no-cost stripping, safe-room macros, deliberate fault farming, duplicate evidence, and client-authored awards.
8. Separate three curves: family handling familiarity, instance familiarity, and gunsmith/maintenance skill. Familiarity may reduce bounded manipulation time, time to stable sight picture, and sway-recovery time; it may not increase projectile damage, mechanical accuracy, ammunition performance, authoritative hit tolerance, or provide target tracking.
9. Route presentation through existing first-person/third-person animation systems. Animation notifies request state transitions but never consume inventory, repair a part, or award progression. Reduced-motion/accessibility modes preserve authoritative time and outcomes.
10. Validate one complete carbine route before expanding: clear/unload, strip, inspect, clean, repair/replace, lubricate, reassemble, function-check, equip, acquire target, fire, induce an evidence-controlled fault, diagnose, clear, interrupt/restart, and repeat with two clients under latency/loss.

## Completion

Report exact C++/Blueprint/Data Asset/animation changes, schemas, migrations, source profiles, profile-index coverage, automation, PIE, two-client, persistence/crash, performance and visual evidence. A JSON profile mapping is contract evidence, not an Unreal Data Asset or playable maintenance route. Compilation, a montage, a disassembled render, or a faster timer alone is not acceptance.
